papers.title_en: GRACE: Controlled Evidence Interventions for Diagnosing and Improving Knowledge Integration in GraphRAG
papers.authors: Minh Pham, Quang Nguyen, Phong Kieu, Cong Tran
papers.evidence: GraphRAG证据干预与反事实鲁棒性评测
papers.tldr: GraphRAG需融合语言模型参数知识与检索图证据，但总体准确率难以诊断失败源于缺失路径、干扰项还是知识冲突。作者构建GRACE基准，在Wikidata上执行LC-QuAD 2.0查询，对证据子图施加断路径、加干扰、接枢纽与反事实替换四类干预。并提出QCFSE-SA，结合类型化局部注意力、全局图注意力和问题条件证据引导与图支持门控。固定生成器时受控状态准确率由57.17%升至62.78%，断路径状态由55.41%升至67.85%。
papers.abstract_en: GraphRAG combines a language model's parametric knowledge with retrieved graph evidence, yet aggregate accuracy cannot show whether failures stem from missing paths, distractors, or conflicts with model knowledge. We introduce GRACE, a benchmark built by executing LC-QuAD 2.0 queries over Wikidata and applying four controlled interventions to each evidence subgraph: severing a support path, adding type-compatible distractors, attaching high-degree hubs, and replacing the supported answer with a counterfactual entity. Questions and option positions remain fixed across the five states. The validated benchmark contains 4,028 questions and 20,140 question-graph pairs. These comparisons reveal that question-only routing cannot distinguish evidence states, while relevance guidance can improve answerable states yet hurt when the support path is severed: relevant facts may not jointly suffice to answer. We propose QCFSE-SA, which combines typed local attention, global graph attention, and question-conditioned evidence guidance with a calibrated graph-support gate. With the factual context and generator held fixed, it improves controlled-state accuracy from 57.17% to 62.78% (+5.61 points; question-clustered 95% CI [+5.04, +6.17]) and broken-state accuracy from 55.41% to 67.85%. Over-abstention on semantic distractors remains an open challenge.

papers.title_en: FIRE-Drive: Feasibility-Informed Risk Evaluation for End-to-End Diffusion Planning
papers.authors: Qifeng Xie, Kai-Yuan Feng, Wenkang Wan, Yue Wu, Maoguo Gong, Kai Sheng
papers.evidence: 端到端扩散规划与风险感知轨迹评估的自动驾驶方法
papers.tldr: 扩散式端到端驾驶规划依赖轨迹初始化、模式评估与监督质量，弱约束噪声初始化易引入不可行提案，几何相似候选间也难区分安全风险。FIRE-Drive提出可行性引导的风险评估框架，结合动态可行锚点初始化、候选特定BEV风险证据及紧凑高质量候选监督与轻量细化。在NAVSIM v1上以ResNet34取得91.5 PDMS，Bench2Drive 220条路线闭环取得71.43驾驶分数与42.73%成功率，统一了初始支撑、风险评分与多模态监督。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion-based end-to-end autonomous driving models have shown strong potential in generating multimodal planning trajectories. However, their performance still depends heavily on trajectory initialization, mode evaluation, and supervision quality. Weakly constrained noisy initialization may introduce infeasible proposals and increase the burden of denoising. Moreover, selecting the optimal mode remains challenging when candidate trajectories are geometrically similar but differ in safety, interaction risk, and progress. To address these issues, we propose FIRE-Drive, a feasibility-informed risk evaluation framework for end-to-end autonomous driving. FIRE-Drive improves diffusion-based planning through dynamic feasible anchor initialization, candidate-specific bird's-eye-view risk evidence, and compact high-quality candidate supervision with lightweight refinement. This design aligns the initial support, risk-aware scoring, and multimodal supervision of trajectory modes under a unified planning objective. It enables the diffusion decoder to focus on refining plausible trajectories while the scorer distinguishes modes using local risk evidence. Experiments on NAVSIM v1 show that FIRE-Drive achieves a Predictive Driver Model Score of 91.5 with a ResNet34 backbone. Additional closed-loop evaluation on 220 Bench2Drive routes yields a Driving Score of 71.43 and a Success Rate of 42.73%. Component ablations and a scorer comparison under matched candidate inputs support the contributions of feasible initialization, auxiliary supervision, and risk-informed selection. Our code is available at https://github.com/Latte00/FIRE-drive.

papers.title_en: Poisoning Attacks and Collaborative Defense Framework for LightRAG-Based Construction Regulation Knowledge
papers.evidence: 针对LightRAG的知识库投毒与图结构层攻击及防御
papers.tldr: 建筑法规RAG知识库的投毒风险缺乏研究，本文在基于英国Approved Documents的LightRAG上开展预注册实验。用150项带安全后果与篡改方向标签的基准，以全因子设计评估文本层、图层、伪造修订叙事和自适应攻击及三层防御。文本投毒随预算升高更有效，图层弱于预期；完整防御达标，但生成层靠69-80%拒答实现，最多损失74点干净准确率。研究表明分层防御须因子化评估，并加入语料准入控制和版本感知核验。
papers.abstract_en: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is widely used in construction, yet the security of building-regulation knowledge bases has received little study. This thesis reports a pre-registered experiment on one fully instrumented LightRAG system built on the UK Approved Documents. Using a 150-item benchmark labeled with safety consequences and tampering directions, it evaluates four attacks (text layer, graph layer, fabricated amendment narrative and a defense-aware adaptive attacker) together with a three-layer retrieval-graph-generation defense in a full factorial design. Text-level poisoning succeeded, with success rising with the budget; graph-level poisoning was less effective, contrary to the registered hypothesis. The full defense met the registered criterion and six of the seven configurations met its threshold, but those containing the generation layer did so by refusing 69-80 percent of poisoned queries, costing up to 74 points of clean accuracy, whereas provenance-based retrieval filtering cost no measurable clean accuracy in the configuration used. A second experimental batch showed that excluding a legitimate unregistered amendment caused no measurable loss of accuracy either, as its wording reached the generator through the graph's entity and relationship descriptions, the route the poison took, which no layer inspects. Interactions were strong, so no layer's contribution can be isolated. A reported zero attack success rate is not evidence of detection unless the refusal rate is reported with it: zero arises either because provenance filtering removes every document outside the manifest without judging its content, or because the system refuses. Layered defenses must therefore be evaluated factorially, and regulatory RAG assistants require corpus admission control and version-aware verification before they can support safety-critical decisions.

papers.title_en: Generalist Action Critic: Harnessing Frontier Models in Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Yun Yan, Shizhi Hu, Zhichao Li, Yang Guan, Shiqi Liu, Jiaxin Gao, Xiangteng Zhang, Wenbo Ding, Jiuhua Zhao, Hui Guo, Xintao Yan, Keqiang Li, Shengbo Eben Li
papers.evidence: 前沿大模型充当自动驾驶决策的动作评论家
papers.tldr: 自动驾驶需提升复杂场景决策安全，现有专用规划器仍有误选风险。GAC以零样本推理时框架，让冻结的前沿模型担任动作评论家，对专用规划器生成的候选轨迹进行复核与重选。在HUGSIM上DrivoR的HD-Score达43.2，三规划器闭环安全提升最高32.1%，NAVSIM v1可纠正52.13%的不安全选择且仅新增0.67%失败。该工作展示了前沿模型与专用规划器协同提升驾驶安全的潜力。
papers.abstract_en: Frontier models have demonstrated remarkable general-purpose reasoning capabilities, opening new possibilities for intelligent decision making in the physical world. In autonomous driving, many recent approaches seek to leverage these capabilities through additional adaptation for action output, particularly in scenarios where existing models underperform. We introduce Generalist Action Critic (GAC), a zero-shot framework that combines frontier models' general-purpose reasoning with the planning competence of specialized driving models through an inference-time harness. In GAC, specialized planners generate multiple candidate trajectories and make an initial selection, while a frozen frontier model serves as an action critic that assesses the selected trajectory against scene evidence and either retains it or reselects from the available candidates. The harness combines camera images with spatial overlays, provides driving context and reasoning principles through textual instructions, and regulates the information available at each stage to support trajectory assessment and reselection. On HUGSIM, GAC raises DrivoR's HD-Score to 43.2, achieving state-of-the-art performance among methods trained without additional simulation data. GAC also consistently improves closed-loop driving safety across three planners, with relative HD-Score gains of up to 32.1%. Experiments on NAVSIM v1 further reveal how GAC improves planning performance by correcting up to 52.13% of eligible unsafe trajectory selections while introducing new failures in only 0.67% of originally high-quality selections. These results demonstrate the potential of harnessing frontier models to improve driving safety through inference-time cooperation with specialized planners.

papers.title_en: AlpaSafe: Risk-Aware Trajectory Selection for Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Qiren Wang, Mingyu Guo, Weisong Shi
papers.evidence: 复用视觉-语言-动作场景表示的风险感知轨迹选择
papers.tldr: 自动驾驶VLA模型每步生成多条候选轨迹，但部署时只能执行一条，现有评测默认使用最优候选选择器，忽略了实际执行轨迹的风险。AlpaSafe复用冻结VLA预填充阶段最后一层隐状态，以轻量头融合候选轨迹，预测相对得分与碰撞/越野风险，并用固定规则剔除风险支配候选。在525个AlpaSim场景上，它优于默认首样本和随机选择，将碰撞有责或越野率从6.41%和6.10%降至4.93%，仅1.7M参数、每决策0.75ms。
papers.abstract_en: Reasoning-based driving vision-language-action (VLA) models propose multiple candidate trajectories at each decision, yet only one is executed. Standard evaluation scores the best candidate, assuming an oracle selector that deployment lacks, and leaves the risk of the executed candidate unexamined. Existing online evaluators typically close this gap with a purpose-trained scene or world model, often rolling out each candidate through it at inference time. We introduce AlpaSafe, a risk-aware trajectory selector that reuses the scene representation a frozen driving VLA computes while proposing its candidates. AlpaSafe reads the last hidden token of the VLA's prompt prefill. A lightweight head, trained on the closed-loop simulation outcomes of the candidates, fuses this token with each candidate trajectory and predicts a relative score and collision/offroad logits. A fixed rule removes candidates dominated on the two risk logits and selects the highest-scoring candidate among those remaining, adding neither rollouts nor VLA training. Experiments on 525 AlpaSim scenes show that AlpaSafe outperforms Alpamayo's default first-sample rule and uniform random selection in selected regret and top-1 agreement, and reduces the collision-at-fault or offroad rate from 6.41% and 6.10% to 4.93%. The selector has 1.7M parameters and takes 0.75 ms per decision.

papers.title_en: STA: A Split Temporal Adversary Method for Evaluating Robustness of Multimodal RL-based Driving Policies
papers.evidence: 多模态强化学习驾驶策略的对抗鲁棒性评测
papers.tldr: 多模态强化学习自动驾驶依赖跨模态时序对齐，细微错位即可破坏融合表示并导致决策失败。现有跨模态时序攻击在通用性、真实性和自适应性上仍有限。本文提出拆分时序对抗者STA，将攻击时机与模态选择统一优化，并用历史状态延迟观测、借助受害者干净动作识别敏感模式。CARLA实验中，STA对PPO的碰撞率超最强基线两倍，攻击尝试少17.8%，并可迁移到VLM驾驶策略，表明时序一致性是关键脆弱点，对安全自动驾驶至关重要。
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal reinforcement learning (MRL) offers a promising paradigm for autonomous driving by jointly leveraging complementary sensor observations to learn effective decision-making policies. However, its effectiveness critically depends on temporal alignment across modalities, making temporal inconsistency a fundamental vulnerability. Even subtle misalignment or latency can corrupt fused representations and ultimately lead to decision failures. Existing studies have explored adversarial attacks to induce cross-modal temporal inconsistencies, thereby enabling systematic evaluation of the temporal robustness of MRL policies. However, existing methods remain limited in generality, realism, and adaptivity. To address these limitations, we propose the Split Temporal Adversary (STA), which formulates multimodal temporal attacks as a unified decision process that jointly optimizes attack timing and modality selection under realistic policy-aware and budget-constrained settings. STA includes two mechanisms: a) a unified multimodal temporal perturbation mechanism that delays observations via historical states, removing the need for modality-specific noise; b) a split multimodal adversarial decision mechanism that jointly optimizes attack timing and modality selection through adaptive optimization while leveraging the victim policy's clean actions to identify sensitive decision patterns. We provide a theoretical analysis of the induced distribution shift and a modality selection principle. Experiments in the CARLA simulator show that STA more than doubles the collision rate of the strongest baseline against PPO while using 17.8\% fewer attack attempts, and that it generalizes to a VLM-based driving policy. These results reveal temporal consistency as a critical vulnerability, highlighting temporal robustness as essential for safe autonomous driving.

papers.title_en: AR-WAM: efficient streaming world-action modeling for autonomous driving
papers.authors: Baiting Luo, Shatadal Mishra, Ahmadreza Moradipari, Nejib Ammar
papers.evidence: 面向自动驾驶的流式世界-动作模型
papers.tldr: 自动驾驶需预测交通演化并快速响应，视频基础模型却因重复编码历史和迭代生成而开销高。AR-WAM结合自回归时序建模与单次前向未来条件，因果视频骨干增量更新视觉上下文并复用计算。它用单次前向获得未来特征来条件化轨迹生成，再用强化学习直接优化驾驶奖励。单前相机在NAVSIM-v1上监督训练达91.5 PDMS，强化学习后达94.0，并在连续驾驶动态场景中保持视觉历史、优于强世界动作基线。
papers.abstract_en: Autonomous driving requires anticipating how traffic will evolve while responding quickly to new observations. Video foundation models offer the first ability, but repeated history encoding and iterative video generation make them costly to use for driving. We present AR-WAM, an efficient streaming world-action model that combines autoregressive temporal modeling with single-pass future conditioning. Because its video backbone is causal, AR-WAM updates its visual context incrementally, reusing past computation and conditioning future prediction on observed motion. We further hypothesize that future features computed from recent observations can improve generalization in dynamic traffic without iterative video generation. AR-WAM therefore obtains these features in one forward pass and uses them to condition trajectory generation, and reinforcement learning then improves the policy through direct optimization of driving rewards. With a single front camera, AR-WAM achieves 91.5 PDMS after supervised training and 94.0 after reinforcement learning on NAVSIM-v1, outperforming the compared strong end-to-end world-action models. In a dynamic setting of continuous driving, supervised AR-WAM keeps its visual history across decisions and outperforms strong world-action baselines.

papers.title_en: AutoE2E: Don't speak - Language free end-to-end autonomy A Real-Time Driving Model for L2++ ADAS and L4 Robotaxis
papers.authors: Muhammad Zain Khawaja, Zaynab El Mawas, Ryota Yamada, Gabriela Cordova, Arseni Lysak, Intisar Chowdhury, Bharat Jayaprakash, Apostolos Georgiadis, Shri Harsha Adapala, Jatin Gautam, Christoph Bank, Alejandra Solarte Uscategui, Atanasko Boris Mitrev, Hassan Ali Ansari, Nishad Sahu
papers.evidence: 多相机BEV端到端驾驶模型
papers.tldr: 端到端自动驾驶模型常依赖语言模块或闭环节评测，开源可复现的基线仍然稀缺。AutoE2E 由 Autoware 基金会 Robotaxi 工作组发布，采用时序 BEV 架构，融合多相机感知、HD 地图与路线条件，并用轻量循环轨迹规划器预测未来车辆运动。模型约 7990 万参数，评估配置中仅约 145 万可训练。在 KITScenes 验证集三秒预测时域下取得 ADE 0.745 米、FDE 2.020 米，并附带检查点、训练评估代码与可视化面板 DataModelConsole。
papers.abstract_en: AutoE2E is an open-source end-to-end driving model developed by the Autoware Foundation Robotaxi Working Group. It introduces a temporal bird's-eye-view (BEV) architecture that combines multi-camera perception, HD-map information and route conditioning to predict future vehicle motion. The evaluated model uses a pretrained camera-BEV backbone, temporal feature fusion and a lightweight recurrent trajectory planner. It contains approximately 79.9 million parameters, of which approximately 1.45 million are trainable in the evaluated configuration. The v1.0 release provides model checkpoints, training and evaluation code, and DataModelConsole, a dashboard for visualizing and inspecting model experiments. On the KITScenes validation benchmark, the fine-tuned checkpoint achieves an average displacement error (ADE) of 0.745 m and a final displacement error (FDE) of 2.020 m at a three-second prediction horizon. The paper also reports preliminary real-vehicle research conducted with the Technical University of Munich's EDGAR platform, alongside ongoing collaboration with the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology. AutoE2E v1.0 is an early open research release. Its quantitative evaluation is open-loop, and the model has not yet demonstrated validated closed-loop autonomous driving. The release is intended to provide the autonomous-driving community with an inspectable baseline for further research, experimentation and collaborative development.

papers.title_en: TrajWAM: Trajectory-Conditioned Future Learning for Vision-Language Driving
papers.authors: Xuerui Fang, Gulimila Kezierbieke, Chen Wangxing, Hui Li
papers.evidence: 轨迹条件化的视觉语言驾驶生成路点
papers.tldr: 面向自动驾驶的世界动作模型需要把未来场景预测与动作规划连接起来，每条驾驶记录都提供了一条已执行轨迹及其真实未来作为监督。TrajWAM 用自车轨迹查询从共享规划器表征出发，预测与 DINOv3 对齐的 BEV 未来特征，并联合训练：在执行轨迹下做事实重建，在未标注扰动轨迹下做单侧特征分离。推理时直接输出路点，绕过辅助未来预测分支。在 Bench2Drive 全部 220 条路线上取得 91.53 驾驶分数和 75.45% 成功率，比调度匹配的纯规划微调基线高 5.31 分、多成功 8 条路线。
papers.abstract_en: World Action Models (WAMs) connect future scene prediction with action planning for autonomous driving. Each driving record pairs an executed ego trajectory with its observed future, providing a factual outcome for learning this connection. We present TrajWAM, a trajectory-conditioned WAM that improves vision-language driving through auxiliary bird's-eye-view (BEV) future learning. An ego-trajectory query conditions DINOv3-aligned BEV predictions from shared planner representations. Training combines factual reconstruction under the executed trajectory with one-sided feature separation under an unlabeled perturbed trajectory. Together, these objectives train the shared planner to generate driving waypoints. Native inference directly generates waypoints and bypasses the auxiliary future-prediction branch. On all 220 Bench2Drive routes, TrajWAM achieves 91.53 Driving Score and 75.45% Success Rate, exceeding a schedule-matched planning-only fine-tuning baseline by 5.31 Driving Score points and eight successful routes.

papers.title_en: What Survives the Shift from Text to Pixels? Conditional Protection against Prompt Injection in Image-Rendered Documents
papers.authors: Haoyang Liu, Yinong Xu, Zhe Lang, Zhenyu Guan, Qianyun Zhang
papers.evidence: 图像渲染下的间接提示注入防护
papers.tldr: 多模态模型读取外部文档时易受间接提示注入，将不可信内容渲染为页面图像平均可降低攻击成功率，但哪些操作仍存活、效用代价及失败原因不明。作者对191个英文问答源的文本与图像版本在六个模型上配对评测追加标记、答案格式化、答案替换和干净问答效用。渲染减少各模型追加与格式化执行，但Qwen3-VL-8B仍以77.96%执行图像替换，防护受目标、设置、措辞和重复影响，八种攻击搜索可补回部分图像缺口。研究说明渲染只提供条件性防护，安全评估应按模型、操作、攻击预算与效用报告。
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal language models increasingly answer questions over external documents, exposing them to indirect prompt injection: commands planted in untrusted content to hijack the response. Rendering untrusted content as page images lowers attack success on average, leaving open which injected operations survive rendering, at what utility cost, and whether failed image attacks reflect unread commands or commands read but not followed. We pair text and page-image versions of 191 English question-answering sources across six models, measuring marker appending, answer formatting, and answer replacement alongside clean Question-Answering utility. Rendering reduces append and format execution for every model, yet Qwen3-VL-8B still executes image-borne replacement at 77.96\%. Protection also depends on target type, rendering settings, wording, and repetition, and a search over eight fixed attack candidates largely closes the image deficit in appending and formatting for Qwen and Gemini, though not for GPT-5-nano. Utility ratios on original questions range from 93.31\% to 101.61\%, but Qwen falls to 61.99\% when answers combine two evidence spans. Illegibility cannot explain all failed attacks: models often transcribe and identify image-borne commands they do not execute, and trusted user authorization raises execution on unchanged pages. Inside Qwen, patching early attack-region states induces all three operations, more weakly in images. Attention blocking suggests why: a text command acts through its own positions, whereas visual encoding spreads an image command and its target across the instruction page. Rendering thus offers conditional protection, motivating evaluations that report security by model, operation, and attack budget alongside utility.

papers.title_en: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Changtao Zhao, Yingxue Guan, Li Wang, Shijie Zhao, Yuhang Zhang, Shengkai Zhang, Qing Wang, Ziying Song
papers.evidence: 面向越野自动驾驶的视觉-语言-动作模型，生成并执行驾驶规划
papers.tldr: 越野VLA规划常因频繁更新反复调用昂贵多模态推理，直接复用旧轨迹又难适应车辆运动变化。FastRoverVLA将视觉规划生成与运动条件执行解耦，用免训练的速度-曲率动作缓冲对齐实测运动，并在每次更新中消费当前动作、回写修正余量。3秒时域下，ORAD-3D与RELLIS-3D的FDE分别降低18.0%和36.7%，请求率仅6.0%和4.8%，还显著降低Qwen3-VL处理成本。
papers.abstract_en: Off-road vision-language-action (VLA) models generate scene-conditioned plans, but frequent trajectory updates can repeatedly invoke expensive multimodal inference. Reusing a prediction reduces this demand while leaving its commands exposed to changes in vehicle motion. FastRoverVLA addresses this mismatch by decoupling visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution. Its training-free interface maintains decoded plans between visual predictions. A speed-curvature action buffer is aligned with measured motion at each update, integrated into a local trajectory, and advanced by consuming the current action. The corrected remainder is written back to the buffer, preserving motion corrections across successive updates. A bounded refresh rule normalizes speed and curvature variations within a newly decoded plan and assigns a short or long reuse budget according to the resulting plan-roughness score. The interface requires neither backbone features nor an additional learned driving policy. Over a 3 s horizon, independent real-request evaluation achieves average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) of 0.328/0.596 m on ORAD-3D and 0.266/0.526 m on RELLIS-3D, reducing FDE by 18.0% and 36.7% at request rates of 6.0% and 4.8%, respectively. These runs retain lower errors across four backbones and both datasets and reduce Qwen3-VL request-processing cost by factors of 16.6 and 20.8 under serial replay, while mechanism and motion-only controls identify persistent state correction as the main source of the observed accuracy benefit. The source code and evaluation materials are publicly available at https://github.com/ADEPT-ORG/FastRoverVLA.

papers.title_en: "More Than You Expect!": Leakage-Abuse Attacks on Encrypted Vector Search
papers.authors: Yang Zhang, Ruiqi He, Xiaoqian Sun, Siyi Lv, Zheli Liu
papers.evidence: 针对RAG向量检索的共检索图泄漏攻击
papers.tldr: 加密向量搜索虽隐藏记录与查询内容，却会暴露跨查询的共同检索关系。作者提出语义邻域泄漏，并设计被动持续攻击 SAGE，基于加权共同检索图推断记录标签与查询类别。SAGE-Dist 仅需类别比例估计，SAGE-Known 利用少量已知标签；在四个文本/图像数据集上均优于对应基线。真实 DCPE 实现中语义泄漏仍存在，说明加密近似检索也有隐私风险。
papers.abstract_en: Vector databases support semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation, but embeddings, queries, and record labels may contain sensitive information. Although encrypted vector search protects these contents, some schemes expose records retrieved together across queries. We identify semantic neighborhood leakage, whereby co-retrieval relationships derived from access patterns reveal semantic categories of encrypted records and queries. We present SAGE (Semantic Access-pattern Graph Exploitation), a passive, persistent leakage-abuse attack that infers record labels and query categories from access patterns. SAGE builds a weighted co-retrieval graph and offers two variants requiring different auxiliary knowledge. SAGE-Dist matches anonymous spectral groups to semantic categories using estimated class proportions and refines labels via optimal transport, without known record labels. SAGE-Known combines graph-based label propagation with spectral-group anchor voting using a small set of known labels. We evaluate SAGE on four text and image datasets. With 1% known record labels, SAGE-Known achieves up to 84.3% mean record-label accuracy and outperforms the strongest corresponding baselines on all four datasets. With only estimated class proportions, SAGE-Dist achieves 66.9% record-label accuracy and 68.1% query-category accuracy on AG News, exceeding the strongest corresponding baselines by 21.8 and 41.9 percentage points, respectively, though performance varies across datasets. Experiments with a real-world DCPE implementation (Fuchsbauer et al., SCN'22) show that semantic leakage persists under encrypted approximate retrieval. These findings expose privacy risks even when vector contents remain protected.

papers.title_en: AgentMoT: An Agentic Mixture-of-Transformers for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Qihang Huang, Collister Chua, YuJie Yan, Shiyu Fang, Zhan Chen, Haoran Xu, Zirui Li, Chen Lv
papers.evidence: 面向端到端自动驾驶的智能体混合变换器推理
papers.tldr: 端到端驾驶模型需决定调用何种能力并判断何时重审决策。AgentMoT 将 Agent、World、Action 专家组合为三条联合训练通路，由 Router 选路，Agent 专家负责推理、技能选择与事件触发唤醒，并按相对能力原则权衡额外计算收益与成本。模型经开环初始化后，以双环演化从闭环经验训练路由、Agent 与自调度器。在 Bench2Drive v0.0.3/v0.0.4 上取得 94.48/92.33 驾驶分和 85.45/82.73% 成功率，验证路由与闭环 Agent 学习的增益。
papers.abstract_en: Driving models need to choose which capabilities to use and when to reconsider their decisions. We introduce AgentMoT, a Mixture-of-Transformers with built-in agent reasoning and system scheduling. Combinations of agent, world, and action experts form three jointly trained pathways for direct-action, vision-language-action, and world-action computation. The Router selects a native pathway, while the agent expert supplies reasoning and selects skills. Execution feedback raises wake-up requests, and the agent self-scheduler learns whether to reconsider the task decision or keep it. Mandatory requests invoke the agent directly. The relative-capability principle guides these choices by relating the benefit of additional computation or intervention to its cost. After open-loop initialization, dual-loop evolution trains the Router, agent, and self-scheduler from closed-loop experience while failure-driven updates refine skills and execution feedback. AgentMoT achieves state-of-the-art results on Bench2Drive v0.0.3 and v0.0.4, with 94.48/92.33 driving score and 85.45/82.73% success rate, respectively. With skills disabled, learned routing improves over the strongest fixed pathway by 1.79 driving-score points and 4.09 percentage points of success rate on v0.0.3. Ablation studies further show gains from closed-loop agent learning, two-view queries, and event-triggered wake-up.

papers.title_en: ROSE-Drive: Runtime Orchestration and System Evolution for Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Qihang Huang, Zhidong Wang, Zirui Li, YuJie Yan, Jingsong Liang, Shiyu Fang, Collister Chua, Zhan Chen, Chen Lv
papers.evidence: VLM驱动的驾驶任务与场景关系编排
papers.tldr: 复杂交通闭环驾驶仍难，仅优化单个端到端模型不足。ROSE-Drive以模型无关框架联合编排冻结驾驶模型、技能、感知工具与反馈控制器，并用蒸馏VLM提议任务和场景关系。它在多个基准积累能力并迁移，Longest6上AutoMoT驾驶分25升至52、SimLingo22升至47，超71%控制步跳过新模型推理。贡献在于运行时编排与离线系统进化结合，提升可靠性与计算效率。
papers.abstract_en: End-to-end driving models have made substantial progress, yet reliable closed-loop driving in complex traffic remains challenging. Beyond improving individual models, system-level orchestration offers a complementary approach by coordinating driving capabilities and computation. We introduce ROSE-Drive (Runtime Orchestration and System Evolution), a model-agnostic framework that jointly orchestrates driving execution and computation. It coordinates frozen driving models with driving skills, perception tools, and feedback controllers. A distilled vision-language model (VLM) proposes driving tasks and scene relations. Shared physical state and persistent tasks support capability composition, task continuity, and adaptive scheduling. The orchestrator combines model and skill outputs across control channels, maintains task responsibility through handover, and uses execution feedback to select controllers, reuse valid motion references, and schedule model inference. Offline revisions use execution records to refine skills and their coordination through a stable task interface. Successive system stages inherit these revisions while model, perception, and VLM weights remain fixed. Evaluations with four driving models on Bench2Drive v0.0.3, Bench2Drive v0.0.4, and Fail2Drive show accumulated capability and transfer before target-benchmark revision. On held-out Longest6, driving score (DS) rises from 25 to 52 for AutoMoT and from 22 to 47 for SimLingo across system stages, while both systems skip new model inference on over 71% of control steps.
